complexity.notes: Variable named `dict` shadows the built-in type; rename to e.g. `counts`. A single pass with a seen-set and early return would be simpler and can exit earlier, and `i in dict` followed by `dict[i]` does two lookups where `dict.get(i, 0)` or `collections.Counter` would do one.
complexity.summary: Counts occurrences of each value in a dictionary during a first pass, then makes a second pass to return True upon finding any count greater than 1. Average time is linear thanks to hashing; adversarial hash collisions degrade lookups to O(n) each, giving O(n^2) worst case.
